executive_summary:
**UPDATE 2026-11-12:** The derivatives clock was reset. On **2026-11-04 NYMEX (CME) consented to a further 60-day extension of the CFTC review** of its Silicon Data H100/B200 compute futures — decision now **2027-01-08**, so the first compute-futures market opens **no earlier than early 2027** (FT, 2026-11-10/11). The CFTC's cited concerns are liquidity and whether the rental benchmarks are manipulable; it plans more work with index providers, and NYMEX's extension is **conditioned on no rival registrant self-certifying or listing a comparable contract**. Capital layer: **Ornn is raising a triple-tranche round at up to ~$1B** (Thrive Capital, General Catalyst in talks), and **Anthropic will not terminate its ~$41.3B Lambda compute deal** despite Lambda missing a Texas lease deadline (Lambda pursuing up to $4B private financing pre-IPO). Spot layer: **RunPod expanded Asia capacity** via an exclusive Japan data-center-onboarding partnership with RUTILEA. Index layer: **OCPI-H100 $3.25/GPU-hr (2026-11-11)** vs Silicon Data ~$3.00 and Ornn $3.37 (2026-11-08) — the ~12% divergence the CFTC now names as its reason for waiting.

**UPDATE 2026-11-02:** Quiet week on derivatives and regulatory layers — CME launch still postponed, CFTC docket CFTC-2026-1850 still awaiting Commission action, no volume/OI figures. Capital layer moved: **Hyperbolic raised $30M** (2026-10-27/29, Walden Catalyst/Lip-Bu Tan), extending the spot-marketplace funding run. **Public neocloud stocks fell >30% in October** — a sentiment overhang that could tighten private GPU-collateral credit terms. Index layer unchanged (four Bloomberg providers + open-source CGI, divergent readings).

**UPDATE 2026-10-26:** The CFTC's RFC on compute derivatives **closed 2026-10-20** with 107 published comments (docket CFTC-2026-1850) — including formal benchmark proposals (NativX COIL/NxCI) — moving the Commission from fact-finding toward a posture on compute-contract listing. The index layer is **fragmenting further**: a new open-source provider, the Computable GPU Index (CGI; H100/H200/B200/B300), joined Silicon Data, Ornn, Compute Desk, and SemiAnalysis, while spot H100 spreads near 4x ($2.89–$11+/hr). Blackstone publicly defended GPU-collateralized neocloud lending (2026-10-21). CME volume/OI still unreported; ICE/Ornn still unlaunched.

**UPDATE 2026-10-19:** The CME × Silicon Data H100 and B200 Rental Index futures **listed and began trading on NYMEX on 2026-10-05** — compute futures are live, no longer pending. First-week volume/OI not yet publicly reported (the validation metric to watch). Architect expanded the AI Exchange with **Liquid Inference**, a real-time exchange for AI inference (2026-10-07, pending regulatory review). The CFTC's Request for Comment on compute derivatives closes **2026-10-20** — an approval/next-step window opens now. ICE/Ornn futures remain announced but unlaunched.

GPU-hour futures are now a listed asset class: CME × Silicon Data slated H100/B200 futures for **2026-10-05 pending CFTC approval** (now live, see update above), Architect already trades compute futures outside the US, and Nodal × Compute Desk entered 2026-09-03. Four price indexes (Silicon Data, Ornn, Compute Desk, SemiAnalysis) settle the same market and **diverged ~$1/hr** on identical accelerators — settlement-index choice materially changes hedge outcomes. Beneath them, 20+ spot marketplaces span a ~25× price range ($0.29–$8+/hr), the fragmentation that indexes and derivatives exist to fix.

**Conviction:** real and verified, but pre-liquidity. **Validation metric:** first-month open interest on whichever contract launches first. **Key risk:** CFTC timing plus index divergence undermining settlement trust.

This is the 1980s oil-futures moment for compute: spot markets existed first, then benchmarks, then listed price risk.
